title: Field Notes
tagline: The odd corners that decide interviews.
story: Past the main journey sit the corners where a senior answer parts from a junior one: how much to let a model think, who may give it orders, where it runs, what it may touch, and what you check first in a system you did not build. Each corner hides one precise detail that turns a general answer into a credible one.
oneLiner: Learn the odd corners well enough to say one verified detail, one failure and one flip condition about each.
youWillLearn: Choose reasoning effort and test-time compute by difficulty, latency and verifiability, and know which values each vendor rejects
Explain the instruction hierarchy and release prompts with pinned versions, eval gates and canaries
Compare prompt optimization routes: hand tuning, DSPy compilers, the Foundry agent optimizer and the retiring OpenAI optimizer
Decide between managed, data zone, self-hosted and on-device models, and map ZDR, customer-managed keys and private endpoints to what they really control
Design text-to-SQL, code sandboxes and computer-use agents that treat generated code and screen content as untrusted
Weigh deep research agents and AG-UI, and explain tokenization pitfalls and the hallucination taxonomy
Answer 'what do you check first in an unfamiliar AI system?' with five ordered checks

flashcards.front: Which OpenAI parameter sets reasoning depth, and what happens with an unsupported value?
flashcards.back: `reasoning.effort` (Responses) or `reasoning_effort` (Chat Completions). Values are model-dependent: GPT-6 Astra rejects `none` with HTTP 400 and GPT-6.1 Sol rejects `none` and `minimal`.

flashcards.front: How many tokens does OpenAI advise reserving for reasoning plus output when you start?
flashcards.back: At least 25,000. Hitting `max_output_tokens` returns `status: incomplete`, which can happen before any visible output while you still pay for reasoning.

flashcards.front: How do you control Claude's reasoning depth on current models?
flashcards.back: Adaptive thinking plus `output_config.effort`. Default is high on most models and medium on Claude Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. Manual `budget_tokens` returns HTTP 400 on Claude 4.7 and later.

flashcards.front: Why can changing Claude's effort between turns raise cost?
flashcards.back: The resolved effort value is rendered into the prompt, so changing it between requests invalidates cache breakpoints. Choose one effort per conversation.

flashcards.front: What did Snell et al. show about test-time compute?
flashcards.back: Allocating test-time compute by prompt difficulty improved efficiency by more than 4x over best-of-N, and a smaller model could beat a 14x larger one where it had non-trivial success.

flashcards.front: What is budget forcing in s1?
flashcards.back: Cut thinking short, or append 'Wait' to extend it. Extending raised AIME24 from 50% to 57%, and s1-32B beat o1-preview on competition math by up to 27%.

flashcards.front: What authority order does the OpenAI Model Spec define?
flashcards.back: Root, System, Developer, User, Guideline, then No Authority. Assistant and tool messages, quoted or untrusted text and multimodal data carry no authority unless a higher level delegates it.

flashcards.front: Does the instruction hierarchy stop prompt injection?
flashcards.back: No. It is a training-time mitigation that raised robustness in the 2024 paper, even against unseen attacks. You still need isolation, least privilege and confirmation of consequential actions.

flashcards.front: What does Azure Architecture Center say to pin and test together?
flashcards.back: Model version, prompt, configuration, orchestration logic and retrieval. Test every change, pin the tested combination and use a router for blue-green, A/B or traffic mirroring.

flashcards.front: Without a metric, can you use a prompt optimizer?
flashcards.back: No. DSPy compilers and the Foundry agent optimizer optimise against a metric and a dataset. With no trustworthy metric and labelled cases, hand tune or build the eval first.

flashcards.front: What side effect does Foundry's agent optimizer have on tools?
flashcards.back: It invokes your agent against every dataset task, so external tool calls run each time. Use test endpoints or mocks. The optimizer is a limited preview as of 2026-10-13.

flashcards.front: What are the sunset dates for OpenAI's Evals platform and dataset-backed prompt optimizer?
flashcards.back: Read-only for existing users on 2026-10-31 and scheduled shutdown on 2026-11-30. The docs warn optimized prompts can perform worse on specific inputs.

flashcards.front: Why is Foundry Local not a multi-user server?
flashcards.back: It is an on-device runtime and SDK on ONNX Runtime, adding about 20 MB to an app. For multi-user serving Microsoft points to vLLM or Triton Inference Server.

flashcards.front: What GPUs and tooling does KAITO on AKS require?
flashcards.back: NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or later (no T4 or V100) and Azure CLI 2.76.0 or later. No Windows node pools, and public Azure regions only.

flashcards.front: Which deployment types keep inference inside a zone or geography?
flashcards.back: Data Zone types stay in their zone. Standard and Regional Provisioned stay in the geography. Global types may run in any region. At-rest data stays in the designated geography.

flashcards.front: What does ZDR change for `store`, and what does it not cover?
flashcards.back: On `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions`, `store` is always treated as false. Some endpoints, such as threads, vector stores and fine-tuning jobs, are not ZDR eligible.

flashcards.front: What does a customer-managed key cover in Foundry?
flashcards.back: Data at rest in the resource's associated storage: project artifacts, uploaded files and evaluation data. It does not cover model inference. RSA keys must be at least 2048 bits.

flashcards.front: Which agent tools stop working under Foundry network isolation?
flashcards.back: Browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are unsupported. Bing grounding, web search and SharePoint grounding use public endpoints.

flashcards.front: How far do text-to-SQL scores fall on enterprise schemas?
flashcards.back: An o1-preview code agent scored 21.3% on Spider 2.0 against 91.2% on Spider 1.0 and 73.0% on BIRD. Spider 2.0 databases often exceed 1,000 columns.

flashcards.front: How should you treat model-generated SQL?
flashcards.back: As untrusted input. The P2SQL paper shows prompts can drive SQL injection in LLM-integrated apps. Use a read-only role, row-level security, a statement allow-list and parsing.

flashcards.front: Which controls matter for Container Apps dynamic sessions?
flashcards.back: Hyper-V isolation, up to 600 concurrent sessions, idle cooldown 300 to 3600 seconds and outbound `EgressDisabled` by default. Treat the caller-defined session identifier as sensitive.

flashcards.front: What safety steps do OpenAI and Microsoft advise for computer use?
flashcards.back: Isolate in a VM or sandbox with no sensitive data, allow-list destinations, treat screen content as untrusted, confirm consequential actions and bound the number of steps.

flashcards.front: Which AG-UI events are mandatory, and how does an interrupt resume?
flashcards.back: `RunStarted` plus `RunFinished` or `RunError`. `RunFinished` with outcome `interrupt` pauses for human input, and the client resumes with a new run carrying a `resume` array.

flashcards.front: How much can token counts for the same text differ across languages?
flashcards.back: Up to 15x with 2023 tokenizers, and over 4x even for byte-level models. That changes cost, latency and the effective context window.

flashcards.front: Factuality versus faithfulness hallucination?
flashcards.back: Factuality conflicts with real-world facts. Faithfulness is inconsistency with instructions, context or logic. The older NLG split is intrinsic (contradicts the source) versus extrinsic (unverifiable).

flashcards.front: Why do models keep hallucinating, per the 2025 paper?
flashcards.back: Errors resemble binary classification mistakes, and benchmarks that reward guessing over abstaining keep them alive. Evaluate so that abstention beats a confident error.

glossary.def: Computation spent while answering, such as reasoning tokens or repeated sampling, instead of during training.
A per-request setting such as `reasoning.effort` that controls how much a model thinks. Supported values and defaults depend on the model.
A test-time technique from the s1 paper: cut thinking short, or append 'Wait' to make the model think longer.
An authority order for instructions. In the OpenAI Model Spec: Root, System, Developer, User, Guideline, then No Authority for tool output and untrusted text.
Deploying a tested combination of model version, prompt, configuration and retrieval together, so no untested mix reaches users.
Sending a small slice of traffic to a new version and promoting it only if its metrics hold.
A framework that compiles declarative language model modules against a metric instead of hand-tuning prompt strings.
The vLLM technique that stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks to cut memory waste and allow more concurrent requests.
The SGLang technique that reuses KV cache across requests that share a prefix, using a radix tree.
The Kubernetes AI Toolchain Operator, a CNCF Sandbox project that deploys open models on Kubernetes and integrates vLLM. AKS offers it as an add-on.
An approved OpenAI data control under which `store` is always treated as false on `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions`. Some endpoints are not eligible.
An encryption key you hold in Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM for data at rest in a Foundry resource's associated storage. It does not cover inference.
A Foundry deployment type whose inference stays within a data zone, as opposed to Global types that may run in any region.
The text-to-SQL metric that runs the generated query and compares its result with the reference result.
An isolated, short-lived sandbox in Azure Container Apps, identified by a caller-defined string, for running untrusted code.
An open, event-based protocol between a user-facing app and an agent backend. It sits beside MCP (agent to tools) and A2A (agent to agent).
Output that is inconsistent with the instructions, the provided context or its own logic, as opposed to a factuality error against the real world.

claims.text: OpenAI reasoning.effort values are model-dependent and can include none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and max. gpt-5.5 defaults to medium.

GPT-6 Astra does not support reasoning effort none and returns HTTP 400. GPT-6.1 Sol does not support none or minimal and defaults to medium. Chat Completions does not support function calling with either model.
OpenAI recommends reserving at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and outputs when starting. Reaching max_output_tokens returns status incomplete, which can happen before any visible output.

On Azure, function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-5.6-sol on /v1/chat/completions, even when reasoning_effort is not sent because the default is medium. Use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to none.

Claude effort is set with output_config.effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). The default is high on most models and medium on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5. Changing effort between requests invalidates cache breakpoints.
Manual extended thinking with budget_tokens is deprecated on Claude 4.6 models and rejected with HTTP 400 on Claude 4.7 and later.
Gemini uses thinking_level. gemini-3.8-flash is on at medium with low, medium and high, and gemini-3.1-pro-preview is on at high.

Snell et al. report that compute-optimal test-time allocation improves efficiency by more than 4x over best-of-N, and that a smaller model can beat a 14x larger one in a FLOPs-matched comparison where it has non-trivial success.

The OpenAI Model Spec chain of command is Root, System, Developer, User, Guideline, then No Authority for assistant and tool messages and quoted or untrusted text. Such content is ignored unless a higher-level instruction delegates authority. The version checked is dated 2026-08-18.

Azure Architecture Center advises testing every change to model version, prompt, configuration, orchestration and retrieval, and pinning tested combinations. Retired deployments return HTTP errors, and deprecated ones accept no new deployments but keep working until retirement.
OpenAI's dataset-backed prompt optimizer is deprecated with the Evals platform: read-only for existing users on 2026-10-31 with shutdown scheduled for 2026-11-30.

The Foundry agent optimizer improves instructions, function-calling tool descriptions and model selection (hosted agents also skills), invokes the agent on every dataset task so external tool calls execute, and is in limited preview as of 2026-10-13.
In the DSPy paper, compiled pipelines beat standard few-shot prompting generally by over 25% with GPT-3.5 and 65% with llama2-13b-chat.
GEPA reports beating GRPO by 6% on average and up to 20% with up to 35x fewer rollouts, and beating MIPROv2 by over 10%.
The vLLM paper reports 2 to 4x throughput at the same latency compared with prior systems.
SGLang uses RadixAttention for KV reuse and compressed finite state machines for structured output, and reports up to 6.4x throughput.
Foundry Local is an on-device runtime and SDK on ONNX Runtime that adds about 20 MB to an app, and Microsoft points to vLLM or Triton Inference Server for multi-user serving.

KAITO on AKS is a CNCF Sandbox project that integrates vLLM, and requires NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or later, Azure CLI 2.76.0 or later and public Azure regions, with no Windows node pools.

Global deployment types may process data in any region, Data Zone types only within the data zone (US, EU or APAC), and Standard and Regional Provisioned types within the customer-specified geography. Global Batch is 50% cheaper with a 24-hour target, and the Developer tier has no SLA or residency guarantee.

Under OpenAI Zero Data Retention, store on /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions is treated as false. Threads, vector stores and fine-tuning jobs are not ZDR eligible, and abuse-monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days by default.

Foundry customer-managed keys use Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM, cover data at rest in associated storage, need RSA keys of at least 2048 bits, and follow the latest version when keyVersion is omitted.
Under Foundry network isolation, browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are not supported, and Bing grounding, web search and SharePoint grounding use public endpoints.
On Spider 2.0 an o1-preview code agent solved 21.3% against 91.2% on Spider 1.0 and 73.0% on BIRD. BIRD reported 40.08% execution accuracy for ChatGPT against 92.96% for humans.

Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions use a Hyper-V boundary, allow up to 600 concurrent sessions, an idle cooldown of 300 to 3600 seconds, and default to EgressDisabled. Doc samples use api-version 2025-10-02-preview.

The Foundry computer use tool is in preview without an SLA, is not recommended for production, uses the computer-use-preview model with access by application form, and should run on VMs with no access to sensitive data.

Claude's computer_toolset_20260801 is GA on the Claude API and Google Cloud and beta on Microsoft Foundry and Bedrock, and Claude 5.5 and later reject the older computer_20251124 and computer_20250124 versions on the Claude API.
OpenAI's deep research models need at least one data source (web search, remote MCP or file search), and its deprecation notice lists 2026-07-23 as shutdown with gpt-5.6-sol as the replacement.

The Foundry Deep Research tool page marks the tool deprecated and cites 2026-11-19 as the o3-deep-research retirement date on Azure. The old tool needed the 2025-05-15-preview API, West US or Norway East, and Grounding with Bing.

In AG-UI, RunStarted and either RunFinished or RunError are mandatory, and a RunFinished with outcome interrupt pauses for human input, after which the client starts a new run whose input carries a resume array.
The same text can differ by up to 15x in token count across languages with 2023 tokenizers, and byte-level models still show over 4x differences.
